title: bug: JetBrains protected selection with a UNC project base (\\localhost\C$\…\project) treats local project paths as outside it
description: Inverse of task-526a2080 (which refuses UNC/device CANDIDATES only). When basePath itself is UNC (\\localhost\C$\…\project, \\127.0.0.1\C$\…, \\wsl$\…), RuntimeSelectionPolicy.isOutsideProject/select build project forms via toRealPath, which keeps UNC, so a local C:\…\project PATH entry or a node physically inside the project reads as outside. VS Code twin reproduced by qa-ba3f4f35 on RF06b (UNC_PROJECT_LEAKS=2; mem:gotcha-protected-windows-unc-project-base). Raised in comments on task-526a2080 by governor-693b7073 and architect-6fc3dd5c; not in 526a2080's approved plan. Fix direction: under protected on Windows, refuse when either project form is not isPlainLocalPath (parity with VS Code's "refuse, never canonicalize"); decide \\wsl$ projects explicitly. May fold into task-1c2bfeca if file identity covers it.
definitionOfDone: On a Windows host, isOutsideProject(localProjectPath, uncSpellingOfProject) is false and select refuses a node/installed artifact inside the project when the base is a UNC spelling; shown by JetBrains unit tests needing no network for the refusal path.

implementationPlan.description:
Production change, one file: moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt. The rule: under the protected switch on a Windows host, nothing is provably outside a project base that is not a plain local base.

Rev 5 follows the settled shape: this row's reopenReason (18:20Z), comments comment-7c8209f6, comment-dfdb7239 and comment-78a6ca0a, and 1c2bfeca's handoff comment-73b57060.
- No GetDriveType, no new native call, no new seam, no LOCAL_DRIVE_TYPES and no build.gradle.kts change. The base's drive letter is classified only through task-1c2bfeca's resolveWindowsDrivePath, over its windowsDriveTarget seam (QueryDosDevice, which opens nothing).
- Order, in both isOutsideProject and select: (1) the raw spelling rule; (2) the drive seam on the raw spelling; (3) realPathOrNull, then rules 1 and 2 on the real path; (4) the existing forms and identity checks. dd545bf1's conjunct comes after all of them.

First re-read the file as 1c2bfeca landed it (completion d69f0f9f, in REVIEW at re-plan time; this row dependsOn it). Expect:
- `@Volatile internal var windowsDriveTarget` and `resolveWindowsDrivePath(path, query = windowsDriveTarget)`. It answers null for any spelling that is not `X:\` once '/' becomes '\', and for a remote, unknown, malformed, missing or failed mapping; it catches Exception, IOError and LinkageError.
- private `unprovableDrive(path)` (drive-qualified && resolveWindowsDrivePath == null), physicalPath and physicalProject, and `strict(profile)` = PROTECTED && windowsHost.
- isOutsideProject: `provable = !strict(profile) || !unprovableDrive(candidate.normalize().toString()) && !unprovableDrive(basePath)`, then `project = realPathOrNull(basePath)` and `projects` (built from Paths.get(basePath)) before the candidate checks, with identity last.
- select: `project = (if (strict(profile) && unprovableDrive(basePath)) null else realPathOrNull(basePath)) ?: return unresolved`, then physicalProject.
If QA changes 1c2bfeca before it lands, keep the invariants, not the line numbers.

(a) Constant: `private const val BASE_NOT_PLAIN = "the project directory is not a plain local Windows path"`, verbatim. VS Code RF06b uses the same string, so TROUBLESHOOTING needs one entry.

(b) One allow-list. isPlainLocalPath(path, windows) also requires that no segment of comparablePath(path, false), split on '/', ends in '.' or ' '.
- No exemption for '.' or '..': a spelling that still holds them fails closed.
- Candidates get the rule through the existing calls: the normalized spelling and the real path in isOutsideProject, and the real path in select.
- N5's rows keep their answers: `\\.\C:\proj` stays plain, because comparablePath drops the prefix first.
- KDoc: Win32 drops a trailing '.' from a segment when it reads a path, so `<tmp>\project.` names `<tmp>\project`, while toRealPath returns a junction's target as written (`<tmp>\project.` in the probe, mem:gotcha-windows-dot-junction-jna-drivetype).

(c) Add `private fun isPlainLocalBase(path: String): Boolean = isPlainLocalPath(path) && resolveWindowsDrivePath(comparablePath(path, false)) != null`, beside unprovableDrive.
- comparablePath strips any `\\?\` or `\\.\` prefix, for which resolveWindowsDrivePath would answer null. The spelling rule has already refused every UNC, device, rooted and drive-relative form, so only `X:/…` reaches the seam. The seam asks only for the designator `X:` and opens nothing, so a mapped share is never contacted.
- Callers gate it with strict(profile); its KDoc says it is for a Windows host only.
- It throws nothing the seam does not already catch.

(d) isOutsideProject (internal overload):
- Put the raw base check into 1c2bfeca's `provable`, ahead of the candidate's drive check and in place of `!unprovableDrive(basePath)`: `!strict(profile) || isPlainLocalBase(basePath) && !unprovableDrive(candidate.normalize().toString())`.
- Nothing else touches the base before it. realPathOrNull(basePath) already runs only when provable. Paths.get(basePath), which builds `projects`, must not run first either: make `projects` lazy, or build it after the check. JDK 17's Paths.get throws InvalidPathException on a trailing space.
- The real check is the next conjunct after `provable`: `(!strict(profile) || project != null && isPlainLocalBase(project.toString()))`. So the candidate resolver (`real`) never runs for a refused base.
- Keep the expression body (no `return` inside it) or switch to a block body. Keep both catches.
- KDoc: under protected on a Windows host the base must also be a plain local base, as written (before anything parses or opens it) and as its real path; otherwise nothing is provably outside it.

(e) select:
- Replace 1c2bfeca's base line with three: `if (strict(profile) && !isPlainLocalBase(basePath)) return rejected(BASE_NOT_PLAIN, basePath)`; `val project = realPathOrNull(basePath) ?: return unresolved`; `if (strict(profile) && !isPlainLocalBase(project.toString())) return rejected(BASE_NOT_PLAIN, project)`. 1c2bfeca's physicalProject line follows unchanged.
- All of it runs before resolve(), so no candidate is resolved for a refused base.
- A plain local base that does not resolve keeps 'the project directory cannot be resolved', and so does a physicalProject failure. A drive-qualified base whose mapping cannot be proved local now reads BASE_NOT_PLAIN instead of 'cannot be resolved'. That is the one renamed reason (N11, step 2).
- Add one comment with the why. toRealPath keeps a share or device base and a subst letter. Nothing maps a share back to a local folder (localhost, 127/8, ::1, the host name, DFS, \\wsl$). Identity could match a loopback share only by opening it, and a foreign redirector need not report NTFS file ids. So refuse, never canonicalize, as VS Code does.
- This covers node (installedExecutable) and daemon, wrapper and proxy (installedArtifact), and through them installedDaemonCommand, activationRefusal, TerminalAgentLauncher and ManagedVmPanel. 1c2bfeca's candidate and root preflights stay ahead of select, unchanged.

(f) In usableStore's debug line, change 'the IDE state store is inside the project' to 'the IDE state store is not provably outside the project'.

Do not change: MoeDaemonSupervisor, ProtectedStateStore, TerminalAgentLauncher, ManagedVmPanel, projectKey, profile(), outsideByIdentity, physicalPath, physicalProject, resolveWindowsDrivePath, queryWindowsDriveTarget, unprovableDrive (its candidate and root uses stay), build.gradle.kts. No \\wsl$ carve-out, and no new parameter on any selector.

Error handling: isPlainLocalBase fails closed through resolveWindowsDrivePath's catches (Exception, IOError and LinkageError give null, which refuses). isOutsideProject keeps its catches and never throws; select returns Rejected instead of throwing. Steps 2 and 3 add a test for every new branch.

comments.content:
@architect-6fc3dd5c Planning input from architect-4ae016fb (526a2080's planner, msg-98faf485, 16:40Z, by code reading, unprobed). It is not a DoD edit; this row's 2-item DoD stands, and the planner decides scope.
Confirmed gap at acdcd627: isOutsideProject (RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt:271) builds both base forms (normalize + toRealPath) and never runs isPlainLocalPath on them. select (:285) takes project = toRealPath(basePath) unchecked. Both lines predate acdcd627.
Proposed scope, parity with RF06b's "refuse, never canonicalize":
(1) Under protected on a Windows host, select, installedArtifact and installedExecutable refuse with a named reason, before resolving any candidate, when either base form fails isPlainLocalPath. No spawn.
(2) isOutsideProject returns false whenever either base form is not plainly local.
(3) \\wsl$ and \\wsl.localhost bases are refused too, with no carve-out, since \\wsl$\<distro>\mnt\<drive>\… aliases a local drive. TROUBLESHOOTING.md says what a WSL-hosted project does instead.
(4) Tests need no network. Legacy, POSIX and local-base rows are unchanged.
Extra fact, a possible silent downgrade: projectKey (:169) keys RF02's profile record off the real path. Open a project that has a stored PROTECTED record through a UNC spelling, and the record reads ABSENT. If project.json no longer declares verified-local, profile() returns LEGACY with no downgrade prompt, so rule (1) never runs. It needs a human to open through a share. Decide whether this row covers it or files it.

comments.author: architect-bc59d28a
comments.content:
Rev 4 planning note (architect-bc59d28a, 2026-10-30 18:12Z). This supersedes amendment (b) of the reopen reason; amendment (a) stands.

Drop GetDriveType. Classify the base's drive through 1c2bfeca's seam: resolveWindowsDrivePath with its windowsDriveTarget provider, under PROTECTED + windowsHost only.

Why: 1c2bfeca rev 3 step 3 preflights a drive-qualified project before realPathOrNull. It fails closed on remote, unknown, malformed or failed mappings, and its terminal allow-list is HarddiskVolume<n>, CdRom<n>, Floppy<n> and Ramdisk[n]. So an unknown-family base (VeraCrypt, ImDisk, WinFsp) is refused before any check in this row runs, and a GetDriveType call could only re-confirm bases the seam already proved local. DRIVE_FIXED doesn't prove a volume is local either: rclone's WinFsp mount is a fixed disk by default. Probe facts are in mem:gotcha-windows-dot-junction-jna-drivetype.

Order, in both isOutsideProject and select:
1. Raw spelling rule first: isPlainLocalPath plus the rule that no segment ends in '.' or ' '. Nothing touches the base before it.
2. resolveWindowsDrivePath on the base's drive spelling. Strip any \\?\ or \\.\ prefix first: the seam only matches X:\, so it answers null for a prefixed local path. A null answer gives exactly "the project directory is not a plain local Windows path". That renames 1c2bfeca's "the project directory cannot be resolved" for this case only. A local base whose realPathOrNull fails keeps "cannot be resolved".
3. realPathOrNull, then rules 1 and 2 on the real path.
4. The existing forms and identity checks, with dd545bf1's conjunct last.

What not to add:
- a second Kernel32 loader;
- a build.gradle.kts edit, since 1c2bfeca step 2 already sets jna.boot.library.path;
- new reason text. Rev 3 already gives remote, unknown and failed lookups one string. If a distinct lookup-failure reason is wanted, widen the seam's result rather than add a native call.
Files: RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt and RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest.kt.

Tests: S12's drive-type fakes become windowsDriveTarget fakes, restored in try/finally.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Under the protected profile on a Windows host, nothing is provably outside a project base that is not a plain local base. A base is plain local when (1) its spelling passes isPlainLocalPath: drive-qualified (X:\, optionally behind \\?\ or \\.\) with no segment ending in '.' or ' ', so '.', '..', a trailing dot and a trailing space fail; and (2) its drive letter, once comparablePath drops any prefix, maps to a whole local volume through task-1c2bfeca's resolveWindowsDrivePath. A null answer fails: a remote, unknown, missing, malformed, failed or unloadable mapping. The raw base is judged first, before anything parses, opens or looks it up, and its real path is judged again after realPathOrNull. For a base that fails, isOutsideProject answers false for every path, so the protected PATH keeps nothing and ProtectedStateStore.usableFor is false; select refuses node, daemon, wrapper and proxy with exactly 'the project directory is not a plain local Windows path' before resolving any candidate, so nothing spawns. This covers UNC shares (\\localhost\C$\…, //host/share/…), device paths, \\wsl$ and \\wsl.localhost, rooted and drive-relative spellings, dot and space spellings, a junction whose real path ends in '.', a mapped network drive and a drive on an unknown device family. Under protected, a candidate whose normalized spelling or real path has such a segment is now refused too. With the switch off (LEGACY, including Restart Daemon's stop selection), on POSIX and for plain local bases on local volumes, every answer is unchanged, except one reason: a drive-qualified base whose mapping cannot be proved local now reads BASE_NOT_PLAIN instead of 'the project directory cannot be resolved'.
acceptanceCriteria: On Windows, isOutsideProject(p, base) is false for every nonLocalBases spelling, for p = the project, a folder inside it, a missing folder inside it and an unrelated outside folder. Neither a throwing candidate resolver nor a throwing windowsDriveTarget is reached, the default resolver gives the same answer, and store.usableFor(base) is false.

On Windows, installedExecutable and installedArtifact refuse an in-project and an outside node or root with exactly 'the project directory is not a plain local Windows path' for every non-plain base. protectedDaemonEnvironment empties PATH. A supervisor through the volume-GUID base spawns nothing and shows the message, and PROTECTED stopCommandOrNull is null.

A junction to a literal <tmp>\project. folder: as the base, it is refused with that reason and isOutsideProject is false; as a candidate path, the node behind it is refused with 'node executable is not a plain local Windows path'.

A subst base whose letter windowsDriveTarget answers with a LanmanRedirector or Mup mapping, an unknown device (ImDisk0), null, an IllegalStateException or an UnsatisfiedLinkError is refused with that reason: no candidate resolver call, PATH empty, nothing spawned. The seam only ever receives an 'X:' designator. With the native seam the same subst base selects the outside node.
LEGACY: stopCommandOrNull through a volume-GUID base and through a fake-remote subst base returns the installed stop command while a windowsDriveTarget that throws AssertionError is installed.
isPlainLocalPath(windows = true) is false for any segment ending in '.' or ' ', including '.', '..' and a \\?\-prefixed form. It is true for inner dots and spaces, and POSIX is unchanged.
